evidence: dead_air: seg4:start to seg4:end replays seg3's identical two-disc picture with only the closing text added, so two beats look the same. seg0:start to seg0:end also repeats the finished hook chart unchanged for about 3s.

weakest_scene.visible_evidence: In seg3:start to seg3:end both discs read "127%" and both are labelled "Billionaire wealth". The title says "wealth vs stock market" and the narration says "the S&P 500 alone grew 195 percent", but no 195% and no S&P disc appear anywhere. The two discs are identical, so the comparison claims a tie and contradicts the script.
weakest_scene.root_cause: The comparison machine got the billionaire series twice instead of billionaire wealth and the S&P 500. Its second operand label and value fell back to the first series.
weakest_scene.repair_goal: Draw two different quantities: billionaire wealth +127% and the S&P 500 +195%, labelled "Billionaire wealth" and "S&P 500". Their sizes should be proportional so the S&P side is visibly about 1.5x bigger. Data should cause the motion, for example by pumping or inflating the S&P side past the billionaire side, so the beat lands the claim that most of this is just stocks.
